events.name: User Input
events.content:
# `--js-version` still lets too-new syntax into minified bundles

We ship a status dashboard to two generations of shop-floor kiosks. The old
fleet runs an Android 4.4 WebView — plain ES5, nothing newer parses. The mid
fleet runs a frozen Chromium 51, which handles ES2015 syntax but nothing past
that. Neither fleet will ever get a browser update; the asset pipeline is what
has to care.

The pipeline minifies every dashboard bundle with the Go minifier checked out
at `/app/minify`, using its `--js-version` flag to keep output parseable on
old engines. The invocations look like:

```
go run ./cmd/minify --type js --js-version 5    dashboard.src.js   # old fleet
go run ./cmd/minify --type js --js-version 2015 dashboard.src.js   # mid fleet
```

Since we moved the pipeline onto this minifier version, both fleets
white-screen on boot: the device consoles show a syntax error thrown while
parsing the minified bundle, before a single line of it runs. The unminified
sources run fine on every device, and the exact same minified files run fine
in current desktop Chrome. QA bisected it to the minify step. Our bundles are
ordinary ES5 — `var`, functions, XHR, DOM calls — nothing exotic; whatever
the old engines are choking on was put there by the minifier.

The flag's documented contract (README: "`Version` ECMAScript version to use
for output, `0` is the latest") means: a rewrite the minifier itself performs
must not emit syntax that the requested ECMAScript version does not have.
Syntax already present in the input is passed through as-is — this is a
minifier, not a transpiler. Some rewrites do honor the flag today; whatever is
breaking our bundles does not.

Fix the JS minifier in `/app/minify` so that:

- With `--js-version 5`, minifying ES5 source yields output an ES5 engine
  parses. With `--js-version 2015`, output stays within ES2015. The same
  logic applies to other version values. Find and fix every rewrite that
  violates this — if one construct slips through, the fleet is down again.
- Every affected rewrite switches back on at the lowest ECMAScript version
  whose spec actually includes the emitted syntax — don't blanket-disable an
  optimization for versions that support it, and don't gate it one edition too
  early or too late.
- Input passthrough stays untouched: constructs that already appear in the
  source keep minifying exactly as they do now, whatever the version.
- Behavior without the flag (and with `--js-version 0`) stays exactly what it
  is today, byte for byte. The gates that already work must keep working.
- Changes stay inside this repository's Go code. No new dependencies, no CLI
  interface changes, and `go test ./...` must still pass.

Before you call it fixed, prove it on inputs shaped like our bundles — plain
ES5 application code — at the version levels both fleets use.
